### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via os audit verify (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os audit verify (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via os audit verify (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via os audit verify (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a217bdf1ccf7960105d90a82f00a18d1f8ec72f4` — the merge of head `6a9dffbae09ceb6fedbee5babc3bc2f901e7165a` into base `bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a217bdf1ccf7960105d90a82f00a18d1f8ec72f4 && git checkout a217bdf1ccf7960105d90a82f00a18d1f8ec72f4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65 6a9dffbae09ceb6fedbee5babc3bc2f901e7165a && git checkout -B drift-repro bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65 && git merge --no-ff 6a9dffbae09ceb6fedbee5babc3bc2f901e7165a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bdd51769ee827b24355fa1328375bb09c05c8d65` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34506 · cards #34165 + #34166 · first review · read 2026-11-16T23:53Z

Head-sha: `6a9dffbae09ceb6fedbee5babc3bc2f901e7165a` (the head named in final-head comment 6933004723)

Read from GitHub at this head (`get_files`, diff, check-runs), not from the report. This is L1 only: L2 and the Tier H human approval are owed separately (below).

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`. The body opens with the attribution lines, then `Fixes #34165` and `Fixes #34166`. Both cards are delivered as their rulings scope them. #34166's ruling (record 6909375840, the maintainer's option A, carried by the fleet) adds no fallback and no API: its work is the `trustedPublicKey` contract sentence, the ADR note and the named test, and all three are here.
- Scope: 8 files: plugin-audit `signature.ts` (new), `verifier.ts`, `bundle.ts`, the verifier test, `spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts` (docblocks only, no type or export change), the CLI `audit/verify.ts` (comments only), the ADR-0154 amendment, and a root changeset. Nothing unrelated, no `content/docs/releases/`.
- Changeset: root `.changeset/34165-…md`, patch for `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/spec`. That is right for `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with `Metadata-protocol: none` (AGENTS.md: a non-protocol change ships `patch`). I checked each sentence against the diff:
  - "The trusted key's type decides the algorithm. A record carries no algorithm field" matches `verifyAuditSignature`, which branches on `trusted.algorithm` from `auditTrustedKeyOf` only.
  - "An ES256 signature is `r || s`, 64 bytes … A DER signature does not verify" matches the length check plus `dsaEncoding: 'ieee-p1363'`.
  - "Fails closed … P-384, RSA, a compressed point, an Ed25519 key in SPKI form … a key whose bytes do not hash to the id" matches the curve check, the canonical uncompressed-SPKI re-encode compare, the round-trip base64 check and the SHA-256 binding.
  - "Unchanged: Ed25519 key ids, the local signer … bundle v1" matches: the 32-byte branch builds the same JWK as `main`, and `AUDIT_PROOF_BUNDLE_FORMAT` is untouched.
  - The switching paragraph matches the new `trustedPublicKey` docblock and the ADR D6 amendment.
- Tests: two new top-level `describe`s in the shared verifier harness, and each live run there is re-judged offline from its bundle. They cover ES256 live and offline, a forged signature, DER refused, the four refused key shapes, Ed25519-under-EC refused, and an id-mismatch refused. The #34166 switch case covers local history pinned, host seals next, all six rows trusted, and a post-switch planted key `untrusted_key`, plus a pins-nothing companion. Three recorded ablations went red (2/54, 10/54, 1/54). The PR body is candid that the first DER ablation stayed green and was re-anchored. The only removed test lines are two import lines; no assertion changed.
- Gates: 68 check-runs on this head: 56 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 1 `cancelled`. Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Test Core 1–8 `success`. The `cancelled` one is the non-required `Auto Label` (PR Automation, cancelled by its own concurrency group), named in the final-head comment. It is for the landing step to clear or account for under the true-green rule; it does not change this verdict.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. `SigningKeyTrust` is the one admission point for the live check, the offline bundle check (`BundleCheck.publicKeyOf` now calls `auditTrustedKeyOf`) and the amendment writer, so no second Ed25519-only path is left behind.
2. `auditTrustedKeyOf` rejects before parsing (empty, non-round-trip base64, hash ≠ id), and its whole parse sits in `try/catch → null`, so a malformed anchor answer cannot throw out of the verifier.
3. The ADR change is a dated amendment section plus italic pointers on D4's signature bullet, D6's seam bullet and the status line. The three removed lines are those three lines re-written with the pointer appended; no decision text is deleted.

**For L2 (named, not REWORK):** the key-id binding (`sha256(bytes) === keyId`) is now enforced for a host anchor too, where `main` did not check it. `main`'s own contract text already defines `AuditCheckpointSignature.keyId` as "the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw public key", and the repo ships no host signer. So I read this as enforcing the stated contract, not a narrowing arm. The L2 record should confirm or overrule that against the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration.

**L2 owed: yes**, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`: `packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts` is a non-test `packages/spec/src/**` path, `docs/adr/**` is governed rule text, and `Clause-②: yes` is declared. Per the final-head comment it has already been sent to the L2 seat at this head.

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34506` reports GOVERNED, `docs/adr/**` ×1, so **Tier H** (+400/−46 = 446 lines). It lands only on an approval from `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` after the L2 PASS. The seat hands it off; no seat flips it ready before then.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6a9dffbae09ceb6fedbee5babc3bc2f901e7165a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts, docs/adr/0154-audit-ledger-tamper-evidence-sealer-signed-checkpoints-amendments-verify.md + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signature.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/verifier.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/bundle.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: cards #34165 and #34166 (bodies and every comment, rulings 6909369413 and 6909375840 included), PR #34506 body and its 8-file list, the net diff against the merge base `24b6ae55`, and the check-runs on this head. Check-runs: 68, every one completed; each concludes success or skipped, except `Auto Label`, which was cancelled and is a labeller, not a gate. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, the `Test Core` shards, the `Type Check` jobs and the `Lint` jobs are green. Remainder at `TIER_DEFAULT` for the lane seat: `.changeset/34165-audit-checkpoint-es256.md` (read for ② only) and `audit-seal-verifier.test.ts` (read only to confirm the pins the rulings name exist).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Verifier accept set widens: ES256 beside Ed25519.** Right. A checkpoint or amendment signed by a P-256 key the anchor answers as its uncompressed-point SPKI DER, under the SHA-256 of those bytes, with an `r || s` signature, now verifies live, in the amendment writer and offline. On `main` every such record read `untrusted_key`. This is what ruling 6909369413 orders, and nothing wider: the pair is closed in `signature.ts`.
- **Ed25519 accept set under the local anchor: unchanged.** Right. `trustedSigningKey` (`signer.ts`, read at head, outside the diff) answers a row's `public_key` only after `unwrapPrivateHalf` has shown it equals the canonical base64 of the derived raw 32 bytes and that the fingerprint is their SHA-256. So every key the local anchor answers passes the new admission rule, and no sealed Ed25519 chain changes its verdict.
- **Offline accept set: widens by ES256 only.** Right. `bundle.ts` on `main` already required 32 bytes, a base64 round trip and the hash to equal the fingerprint; the diff routes the same three conditions through `auditTrustedKeyOf` and adds the SPKI form.
- **The host anchor is now also held to "key id equals SHA-256 of the key bytes" (the point L1 raised, comment 6933043525). Ruled: enforcement of a definition `main` already declares, not a narrowing; no `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line is owed.** The text read on `main` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts`): `AuditCheckpointSignature.keyId` is "The id of the key that signed: its fingerprint, the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw public key", and `trustedPublicKey` answers "The public key (base64, raw 32 bytes) this signer vouches for under `keyId`". The id is defined as the hash of the key, for every signer, with no carve-out for a host signer. A host signer that answered bytes not hashing to the id was already outside the declared contract. Two further readings of `main` agree: its offline check already refused such a key (`bundle.ts`: the hash must equal the fingerprint), so a chain signed that way verified live but never from its own proof bundle, and the diff settles that disagreement on the declared side; and no shipped consumer registers a host signer (the card's Responsibility line: cloud#4128 stage 2, not yet shipped), so no installed deployment's verdict moves. The same reasoning covers the base64 round trip the host path now shares with the offline path. The changeset states the id check openly ("The id check applies to every anchor").
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/spec`: docblocks only in `audit-checkpoint.ts`; no type, export or member changes. `@objectstack/plugin-audit`: `signature.ts` is a new internal module and `index.ts` is not in the diff, so nothing new is exported, as ruling 6909375840 requires (`trustedSigningKey` stays internal). `SigningKeyTrust.keys` changes its value type, on a class marked internal. The proof bundle format stays `objectstack.audit.proof-bundle.v1`. Right.
- **Older readers.** Right. `main`'s offline check requires 32 bytes, and `main`'s live check builds every anchor key as an Ed25519 JWK, so a reader built before this change gives an ES256 key no trust: the fail-closed direction the ruling names.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34165-audit-checkpoint-es256.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/spec`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Correct against AGENTS.md rule 3: no metadata key, value or type changes, so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch`; "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". The CLI hunk is a docblock and a comment and publishes no behaviour. The PR body carries the same two lines. `Check Changeset` is green.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — correct, and the single arm is the right one: the diff's one accept-set change against the declared contract is the ES256 widening; the id binding is enforcement of the definition on `main` (ruled in ①), so no narrowing arm and no BREAKING banner are owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report (#34165 comment 6932342479), `open_questions`: none raised. `security_findings: none` — this review found none either.
- Deviation, "test:repo and the cli integration tier not run locally, declared to CI": answered by the head's check-runs, all green.
- Deviation, PR body opens with the harness attribution comment, and one report for the two folded cards: process only, no contract effect. Accepted.
- PR acceptance note, "live `os audit verify` with a registered ES256 signer is proven at the plugin layer": accepted. `verify.ts` at head passes `kernel.getService(AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_SERVICE)` as `trust` to `verifyAuditLedger`, unchanged by this diff, and the new cases drive exactly that function with a host anchor.
- PR acceptance note, "the amendment writer is not separately pinned": accepted. `amendment-writer.ts` builds its trust as `new SigningKeyTrust(anchoredPublicKeyOf(engine, crypto, this.seal.signer))`, the one admission rule this diff changes.
- Ruling pins, all present in the added cases: forged ES256 fails; DER encoding fails; P-384, RSA, compressed P-256 and Ed25519-in-SPKI keys read `untrusted_key`; an Ed25519 signature never verifies under an EC key; a key answered under a foreign id is untrusted; and for #34166 the three steps the ruling names (local chain, host anchor with pins takes over, old checkpoints trusted and a planted key untrusted), plus the no-pin companion.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or in-app join is added or changed. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts`** — holds against both rulings and against its first consumer, `signature.ts` and `SigningKeyTrust`. Sentence by sentence: the closed pair; the algorithm read from the type of the key `trustedPublicKey` answers, never from the record; the key id as the SHA-256 of the bytes as answered (raw 32 for Ed25519, SPKI DER for ES256); one signature encoding with DER refused; and the pinning duty of a host signer, including that an unpinned fingerprint is untrusted even when its row was planted on the host. Each is what the code at head does. The pinning paragraph is the "contract sentence in the trustedPublicKey docblock" ruling 6909375840 asks for.

**`docs/adr/0154-…md`** — holds against the rulings and against the code. The D4 amendment restates 6909369413 and fixes the three points it left to the build card (key id, signature encoding, explicit key-type check) the way the code implements them. The D6 amendment restates 6909375840, including the sentence that a host may destroy the wrapped legacy private half. The dated pointers at D4's signature bullet, D6's seam bullet and the status line resolve to the amendment heading. One claim was tested hard, "`os audit verify --out` ... lists each trusted fingerprint with its public key": it holds, and holds for a narrowed run too. `readCheckpoints` and `admitAmendments` check the signature of every stored checkpoint and amendment of every sealed object before any `--org` / `--from` / `--to` filter is applied, and the bundle's `keys` is the unfiltered set of keys those records named and the anchor vouched for. So a pin taken from any `--out` run is complete for the records then stored.

**`signature.ts`** (implementing) — agrees with the contract. One key admission function for all three readers; the id hash and the base64 round trip are checked before any parsing; 32 bytes is the only route to Ed25519 and a P-256 SPKI that re-encodes byte for byte is the only route to ES256, so the two encodings cannot be confused with each other and the key's length alone never selects ES256; every other type, curve or encoding returns no key; the verify step is chosen by the parsed key's algorithm and the ES256 path refuses any signature that is not 64 bytes. I tried the usual confusions (a key of one type answered for the other, a non-canonical or over-long encoding of an admitted key, a signature of the other algorithm or the other encoding, an id that does not bind the bytes) against the code as written and found none that the contract says is refused and the code admits.

**`verifier.ts`, `bundle.ts`** (implementing) — agree. `SigningKeyTrust.trustedKey` and `BundleCheck.publicKeyOf` both admit through `auditTrustedKeyOf`; `anchoredPublicKeyOf` asks the host signer alone when one is given and the local derivation otherwise, never both, which is the "no fallback" of ruling 6909375840. Docblocks match the code.

**`packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.ts`** (implementing) — comment and docblock only; both sentences are true of the code beside them.

Nits (no effect on correctness or on the contract as ruled; none needs a fix on this head):

- N1 (nit) — the contract says a key is answered as "base64", and the code admits only the canonical padded spelling of it (a spelling that does not re-encode to itself is no trusted key). A signer that answers an unpadded or URL-safe spelling fails closed with `untrusted_key` on every record. One clause in the `trustedPublicKey` docblock, in a later prose pass, would save the first host implementer the surprise.
- N2 (nit) — the D6 amendment puts in quotation marks D6's "kept for as long as any checkpoint it signed is"; D6 reads "kept for as long as any checkpoint or amendment it signed is". The meaning is unchanged.
- N3 (nit, suggested follow-up for the cloud#4128 consumer) — the amendment says a host may destroy the wrapped legacy private half at the switch, as the ruling orders, and does not say that this makes the switch one-way on that host: if the host signer is later unregistered, the local anchor trusts none of those keys, and the local signer cannot sign while the active key row names a half that is gone (`signer.ts`, `openPrivateHalf`). The permission is the ruling's; the consequence belongs in the host's switch runbook.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-lwtcxr`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmP44onN8RMzsPMqjRq`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Seat record · 2026-11-16T23:59Z · Head-sha: 6a9dffbae09ceb6fedbee5babc3bc2f901e7165a

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：审计封印的签名器接缝在 Ed25519 之外接受 ES256(P-256)。用哪种算法由可信公钥的类型决定，记录里不带算法字段。主机签名器接管后，可以「钉住」旧的本地公钥，旧本地钥签的历史继续可信。
- 为什么改：Azure Key Vault 签不了 Ed25519,cloud#4128 的 Azure 客户没法把签名移进自己的 KMS;而换签名器那天，旧历史会整体读成 `untrusted_key`。本 PR 照你 11-16 的两条裁决做(6909369413、6909375840)。
- 风险与回滚：只放宽验证端。Ed25519 指纹、本地签名器、证明包 v1 都不变，旧链照旧验过。新增一条规则「公钥字节必须哈希到它的 key id」,对所有锚生效(本地锚本来就满足)。回滚即 revert。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signature.ts`(两种编码，失败即拒);`verifier.ts` 的 `SigningKeyTrust`;`docs/adr/0154-…md` 末尾的修订节。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal/audit-seal-verifier.test.ts`,应见 54 passed,含 ES256 与「钉住旧公钥」两组新用例。
- 需要你做的：审批这个受治理 PR(Tier H,改了 ADR-0154)。L1 ACCEPT 6933043525 与达档契约复审 PASS 6933135109 都在同一 head `6a9dffba`;复审判定 key id 哈希绑定是在执行既有契约，不是收窄。批准后席位落地。

席位意见：同意合并。裁决留给本卡的三个点(ES256 key id、签名编码、显式拒收)都在 PR 里定了，并各有消融用例。

## 席位核对

1. 形态：两卡合一 PR(#34165、#34166 同在审计封印验证端),8 个文件 +400/−46;`Clause-②: yes (widening)`,`Metadata-protocol: none`。
